title: MS PowerPoint
summary: Slides, placeholders, views, slide master, transitions vs animations and the show-control keys (F5, Esc, B/W). PowerPoint questions are short-recall - mostly extensions, views and slideshow keys.

subtopics.title: Slides, placeholders and file types
subtopics.concept:
PowerPoint is the Office **presentation** program: content sits on **slides** shown one after another.

**Placeholders** are the dashed boxes on a layout (title, body/content, media) - text typed into a placeholder appears in the Outline view and can be restyled globally. A **layout** fixes where placeholders sit; a **theme** supplies colours, fonts and effects; a **template** (.potx) is a ready-made deck skeleton.

**Slides:** new slide **Ctrl+M**; duplicate **Ctrl+D**; delete with Delete key; reorder by dragging in the thumbnail pane or Slide Sorter. Speaker notes go in the Notes pane below the slide (View -> Notes); handouts print several slides per page (1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 9; the 3-per-page layout adds note lines). Export to PDF, video (.mp4) or images; Package for CD bundles a show with its fonts/media.

**Files:** .pptx (2007+, X = XML), .ppt (97-2003), .potx template, **.ppsx slide show that opens running**, .pptm macro deck.

tricks.title: X-family again
tricks.body: pptx/docx/xlsx = 2007+; ppt/doc/xls = 97-2003; the extra M (pptm/xlsm/docm) = macros; ppsx = the self-running show ('s for show).

example.q: Extension of a presentation that starts in slideshow mode?
example.solution: .ppsx (PowerPoint show).

tricks.title: M for More slides
tricks.body: **Ctrl+M = More slide** (new slide). Ctrl+D = Duplicate the current slide. Remember M-then-D: More, then Duplicate.

example.q: Shortcut for a new slide?
example.solution: Ctrl+M.

mistakes: Saying a .ppsx file opens for editing - it opens running as a show.
Calling a theme a template - a theme is look only; a template includes sample content and layouts.
Confusing Ctrl+N (new presentation file) with Ctrl+M (new slide).
subtopics.notes:
### What PowerPoint is
**PowerPoint** is the **presentation program** of Microsoft Office. Its output — a **presentation** — is a series of **slides** shown one after another on a screen or projector. Each slide holds a mix of text, pictures, charts, video and shapes. Exams test the vocabulary: presentation = the file, slide = one page of it, and the file extensions.

### Placeholders, layouts and slide anatomy
- **Placeholders** are the dashed guiding boxes on a slide layout: a **title placeholder** at the top, a **content placeholder** below it (which offers one-click buttons for table, chart, SmartArt, picture, video), plus header/footer boxes.
- A **layout** fixes where these boxes sit: Title Slide, Title and Content, Two Content, Blank and so on. Changing the layout rearranges the boxes without touching your text.
- **Placeholders guide; text boxes add extra text** anywhere (Insert, Text Box).
- **Slide Master** (View tab) is the top design page: what you put or format there repeats on every slide — logos, fonts, background.

### Theme, template and master — three different words
| Word | What it really is |
|---|---|
| **Theme** | only the look — colours, fonts, effects |
| **Template** | theme + slide layouts + sample content + masters, saved as a file |
| **Slide Master** | the hidden design page that drives every slide |

A theme is a paint job; a template is a ready-made house. Both appear under File, New.

### New slide vs new presentation — the classic trap
- **Ctrl+N** creates a new **presentation** (a whole new file).
- **Ctrl+M** creates a new **slide** inside the current presentation (or use the New Slide button on the Home tab).
- **Ctrl+D duplicates** the selected slide.
One letter apart, completely different jobs — this pair is asked again and again.

### The extension family
| Extension | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **.pptx** | default presentation, PowerPoint 2007+ (X = XML) |
| **.ppt** | PowerPoint 97-2003 |
| **.ppsx** | **PowerPoint Show** — opens already running as a slideshow |
| **.potx** | template |
| **.pptm / .ppsm** | macro-enabled versions |

The X = 2007+, m = macro, t = template rule is shared with Word and Excel. A .ppsx file opens as a running show, not in the editor — a favourite trick option.

### Quick revision
- Presentation = file; slide = one page; placeholder = dashed guide box; layout = box arrangement.
- Theme = look only; template = theme + layouts + content; master = drives every slide.
- **Ctrl+N new presentation, Ctrl+M new slide, Ctrl+D duplicate slide.**
- Default .pptx (2007+), .ppt old, .ppsx opens running, .potx template.

patterns.name: PowerPoint extension family
patterns.howToSpot: 'Default extension of a PowerPoint 2007+ file', identification of .ppsx/.ppt/.potx, or the odd extension out among pptx/docx/xlsx/ppt.
patterns.logic:
1. Default = **.pptx** (2007+, X = XML); .ppt = 97-2003.
2. .ppsx = PowerPoint **Show** — double-clicking runs the slideshow instead of opening the editor.
3. .potx = template; m (.pptm/.ppsm) = macro-enabled. The X/m/t rule is shared across Office.

example.q: A file named seminar.ppsx will —
example.solution: **open directly as a running slideshow** — .ppsx is the PowerPoint Show format, not the editing file (.pptx).

patterns.name: New slide vs new presentation
patterns.howToSpot: 'Shortcut to insert a new slide' or 'to create a new presentation' — with Ctrl+M and Ctrl+N swapped in the options.
patterns.logic:
1. **Ctrl+N = new presentation** (whole file); **Ctrl+M = new slide** (inside the file).
2. Ctrl+D duplicates the selected slide.
3. M is also on the Home tab, New Slide button.

example.q: Which shortcut inserts a new SLIDE in the open presentation?
example.solution: **Ctrl+M** — Ctrl+N would create a separate new presentation file.

patterns.name: Theme vs template vs master vs layout
patterns.howToSpot: A need is described ('same logo on all slides', 'ready-made design with sample content', 'arrange title and content boxes') and the matching term is asked.
patterns.logic:
1. **Theme** = colours+fonts+effects only. **Template** = theme + layouts + sample content. **Layout** = where the placeholders sit on one slide type. **Slide Master** = the design page driving every slide.
2. 'Change on ALL slides in one step' points to the **Slide Master**.
3. 'Ready-made house' = template; 'paint job' = theme.

example.q: Sneha wants her college logo to appear at the same spot on every slide of a 40-slide deck. Where should she put it?
example.solution: **On the Slide Master** (View tab) — anything placed there repeats automatically on all slides using that master.

patterns.name: Slide and placeholder basics
patterns.howToSpot: Direct recall: a presentation is a series of slides, placeholders are the dashed boxes, layouts fix box positions, the content placeholder offers table/chart/picture buttons.
patterns.logic:
1. Presentation = file; slide = one page; placeholder = dashed guide box (title, content).
2. The content placeholder's icons insert a table, chart, SmartArt, picture or video in one click.
3. Extra free text goes in a Text Box (Insert tab), not a placeholder.

example.q: The dashed boxes that guide where the title and body text sit on a slide are called —
example.solution: **Placeholders** — the title placeholder sits on top, the content placeholder below; layouts decide their positions.

subtopics.title: Views, slide master, transitions vs animations
subtopics.concept:
**Views (View tab):** Normal (default; edit one slide), **Outline** (text skeleton), **Slide Sorter** (all slides as thumbnails - best for reordering/copying), Notes Page (slide + notes for print), Reading View (windowed show), **Slide Show** (full screen). **Slide Master** (View -> Slide Master) is the parent design from which every slide inherits - change fonts/logo/placeholders once and the whole deck follows.

**Transition** = the effect **between** slides (Fade, Push, Wipe, Morph - when slide A changes to B). **Animation** = effect **on objects within** a slide (Entrance, Emphasis, Exit, Motion Path). Both are set from the Transitions/Animations tabs; Effect Options and Duration tune them; Apply To All repeats a transition deck-wide.

**Delivery:** Rehearse Timings records per-slide durations; Record Slide Show narrates; Set Up Slide Show handles looping/kiosk mode; **Presenter View** shows current slide, next slide, notes and a timer to the presenter only. Hyperlinks and Action buttons jump between slides or to files/URLs. Print options include Full Page Slides, Notes Pages and Handouts.

tricks.title: Transition = TRansfer
tricks.body: Transition transfers you **between** slides; animation acts on **atoms** (objects) inside one slide. If the question says 'between slides', the answer is transition.

example.q: The Fade effect applied as one slide changes to the next is a?
example.solution: Transition.

tricks.title: Sorter = order desk
tricks.body: Slide Sorter shows every slide as a thumbnail - the view for rearranging, duplicating and deleting slides quickly. Normal edits content, Sorter edits order.

example.q: Best view to rearrange slides?
example.solution: Slide Sorter.

mistakes: Calling object effects transitions - entrances/emphasis/exits are animations.
Editing the Slide Master expecting one slide to change - the master drives all slides using its layout.
Saying Presenter View shows the audience the notes - the audience sees only the slide; notes stay on the presenter's screen.
subtopics.notes:
### The views of PowerPoint
| View | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Normal** | **default** editing view — one slide large, with slides/outline and notes panes |
| **Outline View** | the text skeleton — titles and body text as a list, no graphics |
| **Slide Sorter** | all slides as thumbnails — the best place to **reorder, copy or delete slides** |
| **Notes Page** | slide on top, speaker notes below — printed for the presenter |
| **Reading View** | the show in a small window, for a quick check |
| **Slide Show** | full-screen delivery, one slide at a time |

Normal is where you build; **Slide Sorter is where you arrange**; Slide Show is where you deliver. Views are switched from the View tab or the buttons at the bottom-right.

### Slide Master — change once, apply everywhere
The **Slide Master** (View tab) is the design source of the presentation. Put a logo, set the fonts, choose the background colours or insert a page-number box **on the master**, and every slide based on it updates together. Editing the master is the answer whenever a question says "the same logo should appear on all 40 slides" or "change the font of the whole show in one step". Handout Master and Notes Master similarly control printed handouts and notes pages.

### Transitions vs animations — the most repeated distinction
- A **transition** is the movement **between two slides** — how slide 4 leaves and slide 5 arrives (Fade, Push, Wipe, Morph).
- An **animation** is an effect **on an object inside one slide** — a picture flies in, text dims. Animations come in four types: **Entrance, Emphasis, Exit and Motion Path**.

Memory hook: **transition = TRansfer between slides; animation = object acting**. "Which effect plays when one slide changes to the next?" — the answer is always a transition.

### Handouts and notes
- **Speaker notes** are written in the notes pane (Normal) or Notes Page view; the audience never sees them on screen.
- **Handouts** are printed sheets carrying several **slide thumbnails per page** (1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 9 slides; the 3-slides layout adds lines for audience notes). Print them from File, Print by choosing Handouts.
- **Rehearse Timings** records how long each slide stays, useful for self-running shows.

### Quick revision
- Normal = default build view; Slide Sorter = thumbnail reordering; Notes Page = slide plus speaker notes.
- Slide Master changes every slide at once (logo, font, background).
- **Transition = between slides; Animation = on objects** (Entrance/Emphasis/Exit/Motion Path).
- Handout = printed page with several slide thumbnails; notes are never shown to the audience.

patterns.name: View purpose matching
patterns.howToSpot: 'To rearrange slides, which view is best?' or 'the default view of PowerPoint is' — views as options with Normal, Outline, Slide Sorter, Notes Page, Reading.
patterns.logic:
1. **Normal** = default building view (one slide big).
2. **Slide Sorter** = all slides as thumbnails — reorder, copy, delete in seconds.
3. **Outline** = text only; **Notes Page** = slide plus speaker notes on one printed page; **Reading View** = small-window show.
4. 'Rearrange/organise slides' always points to Slide Sorter.

example.q: Which PowerPoint view shows all slides as thumbnails and is best for reordering them?
example.solution: **Slide Sorter view** — drag thumbnails into the order you want; Normal shows one slide at a time.

patterns.name: Slide Master purpose
patterns.howToSpot: A statement like 'the logo must repeat on every slide' or 'change the font of the whole show at once' — the tool asked is the Slide Master.
patterns.logic:
1. Edits on the **Slide Master** (View tab) flow to every slide based on it.
2. Master controls background, fonts, logos, footer and page-number boxes.
3. Do not confuse: Slide Sorter reorders slides; the master redesigns them.

example.q: To change the background design of ALL slides together, edit the —
example.solution: **Slide Master** — one change there re-styles every slide that follows it.

patterns.name: Transition vs animation
patterns.howToSpot: 'Which effect plays when one slide changes to the next?' or 'flying in a picture is a ___' — the pair transition/animation is the whole question.
patterns.logic:
1. **Transition = between slides** (how the next slide arrives: Fade, Push, Wipe).
2. **Animation = on objects within a slide**: Entrance, Emphasis, Exit, Motion Path.
3. Match the wording: 'slide changes' = transition; 'picture/text does something' = animation.

example.q: The visual effect that occurs when one slide changes to the next is called a —
example.solution: **Transition** — effects on objects inside a slide (a picture flying in) are animations, not transitions.

patterns.name: Handouts, notes and printing
patterns.howToSpot: Questions on what a handout is, how many slides print per page, where speaker notes are written, or which view prepares notes pages.
patterns.logic:
1. **Handout** = printed sheet with several slide thumbnails per page (up to 9; the 3-per-page layout gives note lines).
2. **Speaker notes** are typed in the notes pane / Notes Page view and are never shown on the projected screen.
3. Printing choices live in File, Print (Slides / Handouts / Notes Pages / Outline).

example.q: A printed sheet showing several slide thumbnails with space for audience notes is called a —
example.solution: **Handout** — the 3-slides-per-page layout leaves ruled lines beside each slide for writing.

subtopics.title: Slideshow and editing shortcuts
subtopics.concept:
**During a show:** F5 = start from slide 1; Shift+F5 = start from the current slide; N / Enter / Space / PageDown / Right-arrow = next; P / Backspace / PageUp / Left-arrow = previous; **B = black screen; W = white screen**; number+Enter = jump to that slide; Home/End = first/last slide; Ctrl+P = pen; Esc = end the show. F1 lists all controls.

**While editing:** Ctrl+M new slide; Ctrl+D duplicate slide/object; Ctrl+K hyperlink; Shift+F3 change case; Ctrl+T font dialog; F7 spell check; Tab/Shift+Tab cycle through objects; arrow keys nudge a selected object; Ctrl+Shift+> / < change font size; F12 Save As; Alt+F5 presenter view (Office 365).

| Key | In slideshow |
|---|---|
| F5 / Shift+F5 | Show from beginning / from current slide |
| Esc | End show |
| B / W | Black / white screen (press again to resume) |
| N / P | Next / previous |
| number+Enter | Go to that slide number |
| Home / End | First / last slide |

tricks.title: F5 = Full show
tricks.body: **F5 from the First slide; Shift+F5 from where you Stand.** Esc = Exit. The F-key is PowerPoint's signature - no other app uses F5 to present.

example.q: Shortcut to run the slideshow from the beginning?

tricks.title: B/W = Blackout/Washout
tricks.body: Mid-show, **B** blanks the screen to black and **W** washes it to white - for pauses/questions. Pressing the same key again brings the slide back.

example.q: Key pressed to display a black screen during a show?
example.solution: B.

mistakes: Using Esc to start or F5 to stop - F5 starts, Esc stops.
Pressing B expecting 'Back' - B is the black screen; P is previous.
Thinking Shift+F5 starts from slide 1 - it starts from the slide you are ON.
subtopics.notes:
### Starting and stopping the show
| Key | Job |
|---|---|
| **F5** | run the show **from slide 1** |
| **Shift+F5** | run the show **from the current slide** |
| **Esc** | **end** the show |

The exam trap pair: **F5 starts, Esc stops** — never the reverse. Shift+F5 saves you from clicking through slide 1 every rehearsal.

### Moving inside a running show
| Key | Job |
|---|---|
| **N, Enter, Space, Page Down, Right/Down arrow** | **next** slide or effect |
| **P, Backspace, Page Up, Left/Up arrow** | **previous** slide |
| **number + Enter** | jump to that slide number |
| **B** | **black** screen (spotlight pause) |
| **W** | **white** screen |

N = next, P = previous. **B blacks and W whites the screen** — used when the speaker wants the audience to look at him, not the slide. B is NOT "back"; P is the back key. These during-show keys are a very common one-mark question.

### Editing and building shortcuts
- **Ctrl+M** new slide, **Ctrl+D** duplicate slide, **Ctrl+N** new presentation, **Ctrl+K** insert hyperlink.
- The copy-move family is shared with every Office program: **Ctrl+C** copy, **Ctrl+X** cut, **Ctrl+V** paste, **Ctrl+Z** undo, **Ctrl+S** save.
- Duplicate (Ctrl+D) places an exact copy on top of the original — handy for matching shapes; Copy-paste instead lets you choose where the copy lands.

### Delivery aids the exams name
- **Presenter View** — during the show, the presenter's screen shows the **current slide, next slide, speaker notes and a timer**, while the projector shows only the slide. The audience never sees the notes.
- **Rehearse Timings** — records the time spent per slide for self-running kiosks.
- **Ctrl+L** turns the mouse pointer into a **laser pointer** during the show (Microsoft 365 builds).
- **F1** during a show lists all the show controls.

### How the exam frames these questions
Shortcut questions here rarely go beyond a fixed pool: **start keys** (F5, Shift+F5, Esc), **traffic keys** (N, P, B, W, number+Enter), **build keys** (Ctrl+M, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+K) and the two delivery aids (Presenter View, Rehearse Timings). The traps are always reversals — F5 shown as "stop", B shown as "back", Shift+F5 shown as "from slide 1". Read the direction of the key in the option, not the letter. A quick self-test: F starts (F5 first slide, Shift+F5 here), Esc exits, N next, P previous, B black, W white, M more slides, D duplicate, K linK.

### Quick revision
- **F5 from first slide, Shift+F5 from current slide, Esc ends the show.**
- Next: N/Enter/Space/Page Down; Previous: P/Backspace/Page Up.
- **B = black screen, W = white screen; number+Enter jumps to a slide.**
- Ctrl+M new slide, Ctrl+D duplicate, Ctrl+K hyperlink.
- Presenter View: notes and timer for the speaker, slide only for the audience.

patterns.name: Start and stop the show
patterns.howToSpot: 'Shortcut to run the slideshow', 'start from the current slide', 'which key ends the show' — F5 / Shift+F5 / Esc as options.
patterns.logic:
1. **F5 = start from slide 1**; **Shift+F5 = start from the current slide**; **Esc = end the show**.
2. F5 starts and Esc stops — the reversed pair is the standard trap.
3. F5 in most other programs means Refresh — in PowerPoint's editing view it means the show.

example.q: Which key ends a running PowerPoint slideshow?
example.solution: **Esc** — F5 and Shift+F5 start shows; Esc leaves the show and returns to the editing view.

patterns.name: During-show navigation keys
patterns.howToSpot: 'Which key shows the next slide', 'which key turns the screen black/white', 'jump to slide number 12' — inside a running show.
patterns.logic:
1. Next: **N, Enter, Space, Page Down, Right/Down arrow**. Previous: **P, Backspace, Page Up, Left/Up arrow**.
2. **B = black screen, W = white screen** (pause the visuals); pressing the same key again brings the slide back.
3. **Number + Enter** jumps straight to that slide number.

example.q: During a slideshow, pressing B makes the screen —
example.solution: **turn black** (press again to return). B is a blackout, not 'back'; the previous slide is P.

patterns.name: Editing and build shortcuts
patterns.howToSpot: Shortcut recall in the editing view: new slide, duplicate slide, hyperlink, copy-paste family, or a mispaired option.
patterns.logic:
1. **Ctrl+M** new slide, **Ctrl+D** duplicate slide, **Ctrl+N** new presentation, **Ctrl+K** hyperlink.
2. Ctrl+C/X/V and Ctrl+Z behave as in every Office program.
3. Watch pairs: Ctrl+M (slide) vs Ctrl+N (presentation) vs Ctrl+D (duplicate).

example.q: Which shortcut duplicates the selected slide?
example.solution: **Ctrl+D** — an exact copy appears right after; Ctrl+M would insert a fresh empty slide.

patterns.name: Presenter view and delivery aids
patterns.howToSpot: What Presenter View shows and to whom, what Rehearse Timings does, or the laser-pointer shortcut.
patterns.logic:
1. **Presenter View**: the speaker sees current slide, next slide, notes and a timer; **the audience sees only the slide**.
2. **Rehearse Timings** records seconds per slide for a self-running show.
3. **Ctrl+L** = laser pointer during the show.

example.q: In Presenter View, what does the AUDIENCE see on the projector?
example.solution: **Only the current slide** — the notes, next slide and timer appear solely on the presenter's own screen.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Shortcut to start the slideshow / start from the current slide / end the show', or during-show keys: next, previous, black screen, jump to a slide number.
pyqPatterns.approach: Fix the row: F5 = full show from slide 1, Shift+F5 = from the current slide, Esc = stop. In the show, N/Enter/Space move ahead, P/Backspace move back, B blacks and W whites the screen, number+Enter jumps. B never means 'back'.

example.q: Which key ends a running PowerPoint slideshow?
example.solution: Esc — F5 and Shift+F5 start shows; Esc leaves the show.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Default extension of a PowerPoint 2007+ file', identification of .ppsx, .ppt or .potx, or odd-one-out among Office extensions.
pyqPatterns.approach: The X/m/t rule again: .pptx default (2007+, X = XML), .ppt = 97-2003, .ppsx = Show that opens already running, .potx = template, .pptm/.ppsm = macro-enabled. In mixed-option lists, the lone X-format beats the three 97-2003 files.

example.q: A file saved as seminar.ppsx opens:
example.solution: Directly as a running slideshow — .ppsx is the PowerPoint Show format.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Which view is best to reorder slides?', 'the default view', 'which view prints slide plus notes', or a matched pair with one view on the wrong job.
pyqPatterns.approach: Normal builds (default), Outline strips to text, Slide Sorter reorders thumbnails, Notes Page puts slide above speaker notes, Reading runs a small-window show, Slide Show delivers full screen. 'Rearrange/organise slides' always maps to Slide Sorter.

example.q: To rearrange the slides of a 30-slide deck by dragging, which view is best?
example.solution: Slide Sorter — all slides appear as thumbnails and can be dragged into any order.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'The effect when one slide changes to the next' or 'a picture flying in is a ___' — the transition/animation pair with the four animation categories as a variant.
pyqPatterns.approach: Between slides = transition (Fade, Push, Wipe); on objects inside a slide = animation, in four types: Entrance, Emphasis, Exit, Motion Path. Match the actor in the stem: the slide changes (transition) or an object acts (animation).

example.q: A picture flying into the slide from the left is a(n):
example.solution: Entrance animation — transitions play between slides, animations act on objects.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Shortcut to insert a new slide' with Ctrl+N planted, or 'Ctrl+M does what?' — plus duplicate-slide questions.
pyqPatterns.approach: Ctrl+M = new slide inside the file; Ctrl+N = new presentation file; Ctrl+D = duplicate the selected slide. The Home tab's New Slide button does Ctrl+M's job with the mouse.

example.q: The shortcut to insert a new slide is:
example.solution: Ctrl+M — Ctrl+N creates a separate new presentation.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A scenario: 'same logo on all slides', 'change fonts of the whole deck', 'ready-made design with sample content' — which feature fits?
pyqPatterns.approach: Slide Master repeats edits on every slide (logo, fonts, background, footer); theme = look only; template = theme + layouts + sample content; layout = placeholder arrangement of one slide type. 'In one step for all slides' points to the master.

example.q: Where should a college logo be placed so that it appears on every slide?
example.solution: On the Slide Master — everything there repeats on all slides based on it.

solvedExamples.q: Which function key starts a slide show from the beginning in MS PowerPoint?
solvedExamples.solution: F5 runs the slideshow from slide 1 (Shift+F5 starts from the current slide). F7 checks spelling, F12 is Save As, F2 has no presentation role.
solvedExamples.shortcut: F5 = Full show from the First slide.

solvedExamples.q: The effect that controls how one slide is replaced by the next slide is called:
solvedExamples.solution: Transitions govern slide-to-slide changeover (Fade, Push, Wipe). Animations act on individual objects inside a slide - entrance, emphasis, exit, motion paths.
solvedExamples.shortcut: 'Between two slides' -> transition; 'within one slide' -> animation.

solvedExamples.q: During a running slide show, pressing the B key:
options: Turns the screen black until pressed again
solvedExamples.solution: B blanks the screen to black (useful while discussing or pausing); pressing B again restores the slide. Esc ends the show, P moves to the previous slide.
solvedExamples.shortcut: B = Blackout, W = Washout. Neither navigates.

solvedExamples.q: In which view can all slides be seen together as thumbnails for easy rearranging?
solvedExamples.solution: Slide Sorter displays the whole deck as miniature slides, making reorder, duplicate and delete operations quick. Normal view edits a single slide's content.
solvedExamples.shortcut: 'See all slides together / rearrange' = Slide Sorter, word for word.

practice.q: The default file extension of a PowerPoint 2019 presentation is:
practice.solution: PowerPoint 2007 onwards saves as .pptx (Office Open XML). .ppt is the 97-2003 format, .potx is a template, .ppsx is a show file.
practice.shortcut: X = XML = 2007+, same rule as docx/xlsx.

practice.q: A file saved as .ppsx:
options: Opens directly as a running slide show
practice.solution: The .ppsx 'PowerPoint show' launches straight into the slideshow when double-clicked; to edit it, open PowerPoint first and browse to the file.

practice.q: The dashed boxes on a slide that hold the title or body text are called:
practice.solution: Placeholders are the pre-formatted containers (title, content, media) defined by the slide layout; text typed into them feeds the Outline view.
practice.shortcut: Presentation-speak: layout defines placeholders; theme defines colours.

practice.q: Which shortcut inserts a new slide in the open presentation?
practice.solution: Ctrl+M adds a new slide. Ctrl+N creates a whole new presentation file; Ctrl+D duplicates the selected slide/object; Ctrl+S saves.
practice.shortcut: M for More slide; N gives a new FILE, not a slide.

practice.q: Shift+F5 in MS PowerPoint:
options: Starts the show from the currently selected slide
practice.solution: Shift+F5 runs the presentation from the slide you are currently editing - handy while testing a single slide. F5 alone always starts from the first slide.

practice.q: Which key combination ends a running slide show?
practice.solution: Esc exits the slideshow back to the editor (Alt+F4 would close PowerPoint itself; F5 starts a show).
practice.shortcut: Presenting runs until Escape - the universal cancel key.

practice.q: To change the font, colour scheme and logo position on every slide at once, edit the:
practice.solution: The Slide Master is the parent design; changes there cascade to every slide built on its layouts - the standard way to rebrand a deck globally.
practice.shortcut: 'Every slide at once' = Master (slide master for slides, handout master for printouts).

practice.q: Entrance, Emphasis, Exit and Motion Path are categories of:
practice.solution: These four are animation effect types acting on objects within a slide. Transitions only control slide-to-slide changeover.
practice.shortcut: Object effects = animation (the 4 categories listed); slide changeover = transition.

practice.q: Which view prints one slide at the top with the speaker's notes below?
practice.solution: Notes Page view (and its print option) shows the slide above and its notes beneath - used while preparing to speak.
practice.shortcut: Slide on top, notes underneath = Notes Page.

practice.q: The Rehearse Timings feature is used to:
options: Record the time spent on each slide for automatic advance
Time the download of the file
practice.solution: Rehearse Timings records how long each slide stays on screen while you practise, then can auto-advance the show using those durations - essential for self-running kiosks.
practice.shortcut: Practise now, auto-advance later - that is Rehearse Timings.

practice.q: Handouts printed with the '3 slides' layout are popular because:
options: Lines for audience notes appear beside each slide
They include the full speaker notes
practice.solution: The 3-slides-per-page handout prints each slide with ruled lines beside it so the audience can take notes. Speaker notes are NOT included (that is the Notes Pages layout).
practice.shortcut: 3-up = slides + note lines; Notes Pages = slide + your notes.

practice.q: In a running show, which key sequence jumps directly to slide number 7?
practice.solution: Type the slide number and press Enter to jump straight there during a show (works up to the deck's length).
practice.shortcut: Type-and-Enter is the show's hidden navigator; Home/End only reach first/last.

practice.q: Which Office-wide shortcut opens the Font dialog box in PowerPoint?
practice.solution: Ctrl+T opens the Font dialog (face, style, size, effects) in PowerPoint. Ctrl+F is Find; Ctrl+D duplicates the selected slide/object.
practice.shortcut: In PPT, T = Type(faces): Ctrl+T is the font box.

practice.q: Presenter View during a slideshow shows the presenter:
options: Only the current slide, like the audience
Current slide, next slide, notes and a timer
practice.solution: Presenter View (Alt+F5, or enabled in Slide Show settings with two displays) gives the speaker the current slide, a peek at the next, speaker notes and a clock/timer, while the audience sees only the slide.
practice.shortcut: Presenter gets a dashboard; audience gets the slide - nothing else.

practice.q: The default file extension of a PowerPoint 2007 or later presentation is —
practice.solution: **.pptx** is the Office Open XML default (X = XML). .ppt is 97-2003, .ppsx is a show, .potx is a template.

practice.q: Double-clicking a .ppsx file in Windows Explorer will —
options: Open it for editing in Normal view
Start playing it as a slideshow
practice.solution: **.ppsx = PowerPoint Show** — it opens running as a show, ready for the audience, not in the editor.

practice.q: Which extension belongs to a PowerPoint template?
practice.solution: **t = template**: .potx (plain) and .potm (with macros).

practice.q: Which option is the odd one out?
practice.solution: .ppt, .doc and .xls are all pre-2007 binary formats; **.pptx** alone is a 2007+ Office Open XML file.

practice.q: Which shortcut key inserts a new slide into the current presentation?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+M = new slide**; Ctrl+N would open a whole new presentation file.

practice.q: Pressing Ctrl+N inside PowerPoint creates —
practice.solution: **Ctrl+N = new presentation** (a separate file). The new slide key is Ctrl+M.

practice.q: A theme in PowerPoint controls —
practice.solution: A **theme is only the look**. A template additionally carries layouts, masters and sample content.

practice.q: Which design choice fixes where the title and content boxes sit on a slide?
practice.solution: A **layout** positions the placeholders (Title Slide, Title and Content, Blank...).

practice.q: A PowerPoint presentation is a collection of —
practice.solution: The presentation file is a sequence of **slides** shown one after another.

practice.q: The one-click buttons inside a content placeholder insert —
options: A table, chart, SmartArt, picture or video
practice.solution: The **content placeholder's icon row** drops any of these objects straight into the box.

practice.q: Free text placed anywhere on a slide needs which tool?
practice.solution: **Insert, Text Box** puts a movable text container anywhere; placeholders stay in their layout positions.

practice.q: Match: 1. Ctrl+M 2. Ctrl+N 3. Ctrl+D — a. new presentation b. duplicate slide c. new slide
practice.solution: Ctrl+M = new slide, Ctrl+N = new presentation, Ctrl+D = duplicate the selected slide.
practice.shortcut: M slide, N file, D duplicate.

practice.q: The default view of PowerPoint while editing is —
practice.solution: **Normal view** shows one large slide with the slides/outline and notes panes around it.

practice.q: Ravi wants to rearrange 30 slides by dragging. The best view is —
practice.solution: **Slide Sorter** shows every slide as a thumbnail, so reordering, copying and deleting take seconds.

practice.q: Which view shows only the text (titles and body) of all slides as a list?
practice.solution: **Outline view** strips graphics and shows the text skeleton — quick for fixing wording and order.

practice.q: Which view prints one slide at the top with the speaker notes below it?
practice.solution: **Notes Page** lays out the slide above its notes — designed for the presenter's printout.

practice.q: Changes made on the Slide Master affect —
options: All slides based on that master
practice.solution: The **master drives the design of every slide** that follows it — logo, fonts and background included.

practice.q: Which view should Meena open to insert her institute's name at the bottom of every slide at once?
practice.solution: Footers, logos and page numbers belong on the **Slide Master** — set once, visible everywhere.

practice.q: The effect shown when one slide changes to the next is a —
practice.solution: Slide-to-slide movements (Fade, Push, Wipe) are **transitions**.

practice.q: A picture flying into a slide from the left is an example of —
practice.solution: Effects **on objects** are animations; 'flying in' is an **Entrance** animation. Transitions act between slides.

practice.q: The four categories of PowerPoint animations are —
practice.solution: Animations come in **Entrance** (arrive), **Emphasis** (highlight), **Exit** (leave) and **Motion Path** (move along a line).

practice.q: Which statement is correct?
options: Transitions play between slides; animations play on objects
Animations play between slides; transitions play on objects
Transitions and animations are the same feature
practice.solution: The core distinction: **between slides = transition; inside a slide = animation**.

practice.q: A handout in PowerPoint is —
options: The first slide of a show
A printed sheet with several slide thumbnails per page
practice.solution: **Handouts** print 1-9 slide thumbnails per page for the audience to keep.

practice.q: Where are speaker notes typed so that the audience never sees them on screen?
options: In the notes pane / Notes Page view
practice.solution: Notes live under the slide in **Normal** or in **Notes Page** view — they are projected never.

practice.q: Which key starts a PowerPoint slideshow from the FIRST slide?
practice.solution: **F5 = full show from slide 1.** Shift+F5 starts from the current slide; Esc stops.

practice.q: To rehearse from slide 12 without replaying slides 1-11, press —
practice.solution: **Shift+F5 runs the show from the slide you are on** — a rehearsal time-saver.

practice.q: A running slideshow is closed with —
practice.solution: **Esc exits the show** and returns to Normal editing view.

practice.q: Which pair is correctly matched?
options: Esc — start the show from current slide
practice.solution: F5 starts, Shift+F5 starts from the current slide, Esc stops — the reversed options are all traps.

practice.q: During a slideshow, which key moves to the NEXT slide?
practice.solution: **N = next** (Enter, Space and Page Down also work); P = previous.

practice.q: During a show, the speaker wants the audience to look at him, not the slide. He presses —
options: B to black out the screen
practice.solution: **B blanks the screen to black** (W makes it white); pressing B again restores the slide.

practice.q: To jump directly to slide 15 during a show, press —
practice.solution: **Number + Enter** teleports the show to that slide number.

practice.q: Which key does NOT advance to the next slide during a show?
practice.solution: Space, Enter and Page Down all advance; **B only blacks the screen**.

practice.q: Which shortcut inserts a hyperlink in PowerPoint?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+K = hyperlink** in every Office program. Ctrl+M is new slide, Ctrl+H opens Replace.

practice.q: Ctrl+D in PowerPoint duplicates —
practice.solution: **Ctrl+D = duplicate** whatever is selected — a slide, a shape or a picture.

practice.q: Presenter View gives the presenter —
options: Current slide, next slide, notes and a timer
practice.solution: **Presenter View** is the speaker's private dashboard; the projector shows only the slide.

practice.q: Which feature records the time spent on each slide for a self-running show?
practice.solution: **Rehearse Timings** (Slide Show tab) records per-slide seconds so the show can run unattended.
